annotations.rationale: In the title, this canonical disease name refers to the disease under study rather than to a generic disease category.
This is a contextually narrowed, recognized form of phenylketonuria; the modifier 'Classical' is needed for the most specific disease span.
This phrase is used definitionally to describe a genetic disease type/family, not a particular instantiated diagnosis.
This deficit phrase denotes the pathological PAH deficiency state causing the disorder, not merely a laboratory finding, and the 'of ...' complement is required to identify the deficiency.
This abbreviation is used referentially for phenylketonuria in the disease discussion, and synonymous abbreviated mentions are annotated separately.
This plural mention refers generically to phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency states/disorders as a class associated with different genotypes, not to one specific diagnosis.
